notable_absence.finding: manage-links.md never names a SQL++ CREATE LINK / ALTER LINK / DROP LINK statement anywhere, and never cross-references 5_ddl.md for a specific statement - a sharp asymmetry with its sibling manage-datasets.json (this batch), where every collection action (create, map, connect, disconnect, delete) explicitly names and links to the equivalent DDL statement. Every 'you can also do this' cross-reference on this page ('You can also create a remote link using the command-line interface or the REST API', repeated six times for create/edit/delete across remote/S3/Azure/GCS link types) points only to the CLI (couchbase-cli analytics-link-setup) or the REST API, never to a SQL++ statement. Either links have no dedicated SQL++ DDL statement at all (unlike collections, which do), or this page simply never mentions one - the round brief's sibling batch reading 5_ddl.md directly is better placed to settle which.

cross_component_finding: The remote-link connectivity requirements name four TCP ports by two names each (mgmt/rest_port, mgmtSSL/ssl_rest_port, kv/memcached_port, kvSSL/memcached_ssl_port), and one of them - 18091 - is already a promoted concept (port:18091, 'the TLS-secured Couchbase Web Console / Cluster Manager REST port') minted from an unrelated context (Web Console access). This page confirms the same physical port serves a second, structurally distinct role: the secure management-API port a remote Couchbase cluster's node must expose for an Analytics remote link to connect to it, independent of any Web Console access.
cross_product_finding: capella:analytics-external-link (Capella, cloud/clusters/analytics-service/analytics-links.json, unpromoted) is defined almost word-for-word identically to this page's analytics:external-link ('a link to an external data source (Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob)'), and the S3/Azure/GCS security caution on this page ('Root account credentials should never be used ... grant the minimum possible permissions') closely echoes Capella's own IAM caution on the same feature - yet neither page states the two external-link mechanisms are the same, and no page anywhere states that Server's own remote-link connectivity model (ports, encryption modes, SCRAM-SHA) has any Capella counterpart at all. Kept separate per the no-silent-merge rule; a strong reconciliation candidate given the near-verbatim external-link overlap.
